The FOMC’s March 2017 statement is modestly hawkish—acknowledging solid job gains, a moderate expansion, inflation moving toward 2%, and a 25 bp hike while keeping policy accommodative via reinvestment and forward guidance. However, the SLOOS tempers that tone: banks reported C&I standards largely unchanged but expect to ease somewhat for C&I and certain residential mortgage categories, while anticipating tighter standards for CRE, construction/land development, and auto loans. Banks also expect asset quality to deteriorate in credit cards, autos, and multifamily, and foreign banks report weaker business loan demand with plans to tighten C&I and CRE standards. Netting these signals, credit supply looks mixed with tightening in riskier segments and some easing in safer ones, implying headwinds that moderate the hawkish read of the statement.
